why: This is not a review loop. Each of the six answered dispatches (rounds 1, 2, 3, 9, 10, 11) was a FIRST read of a different source's notes, every finding is NEW, nothing is REPEATED, REVERSING or oscillating, and no source has had a second round. The cap fired only because the counter counted those first reads despite saying it exempts them. Nothing in owes-round.diff causes the twelve owed keys (the diff is empty since the last round): they are owed because six cited sources (shugiin-1950-genmai-koku, shugiin-1950-genmai-koku-question, maff-2023-genmai-density, koku-enwiki, kokudaka-jawiki, l7r-budgets) have never been read at all. Accepting would close a sourcing question with half its citations unchecked, which is not 'good enough' for a record whose purpose is checked sources.
what: This ruling allows the one round of FIRST reads that is owed: one source-reader dispatch for each of the six never-read sources, each from its existing `make check-bundle KEY=<k> WHOLE=1` bundle (sr-shugiin-1950-genmai-koku, sr-shugiin-1950-genmai-koku-question, sr-maff-2023-genmai-density, sr-koku-enwiki, sr-kokudaka-jawiki, sr-l7r-budgets), sent as one wave. Since l7r-budgets is on GitHub, refetch it from raw.githubusercontent.com first (round 11 found the blob page empty). Apply the findings already in hand (round 1's shogunate clause and kyomasu-jawiki citation; round 2's 'not every domain' scope; round 3's 'three of them' and the shogunate-only scope; round 11's l7r-money anchor and the 2-koku 'need' explanation) along with these. No second read of any of the six already-read sources: their findings get fixed or filed as rows, not rechecked. If a second-read round comes up later, it goes to the cap as normal.
tooling_fix: In hm_checks.py, the source-reader round counter must not count a dispatch whose owed keys (0248#<key>) have no earlier kept reply in the feature (a first read of that source), so per-source first reads of a new question stop filling ROUND_CAP; and make source-pages must fetch raw.githubusercontent.com for github.com/.../blob/ URLs.
